messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — after we flipped the new outbound proxy chain this morning, our app is getting intermittent 502/403 from Redwood API. Started ~08:10 local. No changes on our app side.

maya_support: Sorry you're seeing that. Can you paste a minimal repro curl + verbose output? Also which deployment (Private VPC / Dedicated / Hosted)?

acme_ops: Private (VPC) deployment. Here's a quick curl we ran from the app host behind corp proxies (we use chained PAC -> authenticating forward proxy -> TLS-inspecting gateway):

acme_ops: ```
curl -v -x http://corp-proxy:8080 -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate
* About to connect() to corp-proxy port 8080 (#0)
* Connected to corp-proxy (10.10.2.5) port 8080 (#0)
* Establish HTTP proxy tunnel to api.redwood-inference.internal:443
> CONNECT api.redwood-inference.internal:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-inference.internal:443
> Proxy-Authorization: Basic ****
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* CONNECT phase completed; starting SSL/TLS handshake
* error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'api.redwood-inference.internal'
* Failed to connect to api.redwood-inference.internal:443
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL connect error
```

maya_support: Thanks — helpful. Two quick notes: 1) that SSL alert + CN mismatch looks like TLS interception (MITM) altering certs or SNI rewrite, 2) the CONNECT returned 200 but handshake failed, so proxy allows CONNECT but is doing TLS inspect or rewriting host header.

jorge_infra: Also could be DNS split-horizon — if the proxy resolves to an internal load balancer IP without the expected cert SAN. Can you paste `nslookup api.redwood-inference.internal` and `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.internal` output?

acme_ops: Sure. nslookup returns 172.31.45.11 (internal egress IP). openssl shows certificate CN=corp-proxy-inspect.local and SAN includes corp-proxy-inspect.local only.

elaine_support: That confirms TLS inspection is active. For Private VPC we recommend either:  - Allow TLS passthrough for api.redwood-inference.* hosts (no MITM), or  - Add Redwood's CA/public cert to your proxy trust store so certs match, or  - Use allocated egress IPs and whitelist them so you can avoid inspection.

acme_ops: We tried adding an allow rule for *.redwood-inference.internal but proxy still intercepts. Our security team enforces inspection for all outbound TLS except explicitly exempted hosts.

maya_support: Two operational checks to request from security team: 1) Ensure the proxy preserves SNI (some TLS-inspectors rewrite SNI to internal name) and 2) Ensure CONNECT to port 443 is a raw tunnel (no SSL termination). If you must keep inspection, add a policy exception for `api.redwood-inference.internal`/`*.redwood-inference.internal` to bypass inspection.

acme_ops: Also seeing occasional 401s in our app logs: token validation fails only when requests go through proxy. Same request from a host with direct internet returns 200. Could the proxy be stripping or altering Authorization headers?

jorge_infra: Yep — some proxies strip Authorization on CONNECT->HTTP translations or rewrite headers when doing man-in-the-middle. Check proxy ACLs for header removal and ensure `Proxy-Authorization` vs `Authorization` handling is correct. Also check that your app isn't using preemptive auth that the proxy converts.

acme_ops: Security says header stripping is default for our gateway but they can add exceptions. Before we change prod rules, can we get a short checklist so we can reproduce in staging and validate?

maya_support: Repro checklist: 1) From staging host behind same proxy chain, run the curl above and capture full `-v` output. 2) Run `openssl s_client -connect <resolved-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.internal -showcerts` and confirm cert SANs. 3) tcpdump a few packets during the failed handshake to confirm SNI in cleartext vs rewritten. 4) Check proxy logs for header normalization and any `Authorization` removal rules. 5) If you have egress allowlist, ensure staging IP is allowed. 6) Try a direct outbound test from a non-inspected host (control) to confirm token/behavior.

acme_ops: Doing that now. Quick question: are there specific domains or IPs we should ask security to whitelist?

elaine_support: For Private customers we publish egress IP ranges in the Console (under Org -> Networking -> Egress IPs). Also whitelist `api.redwood-inference.internal` + any model-serving subdomains shown in your config. If you need a short-term bypass, add `api.redwood-inference.internal:443` to TLS passthrough exception.

sre-bot: [alert] repeated connection failures detected from acme-prod-vpc to api.redwood-inference.internal between 08:09 and 08:17. Incident ticket: #INC-2026 created.

acme_ops: Followed checklist. Findings: 1) tcpdump shows client hello SNI=api.redwood-inference.internal, but inspector rewrites TLS and presents its own cert. 2) Proxy log shows `AuthHeaderStrip=true` for CONNECT flows. 3) After security added header-preserve exception and a passthrough rule for the host, curl successes returned 200 and app requests green.

maya_support: Great — sounds like resolution path is confirmed. If you'd like, we can validate with a small traffic sample from our side once you re-enable prod traffic.

acme_ops: Please do. We'll keep prod in passthrough for the next hour and run smoke load. Will post results here. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

elaine_support: One more note for future: if your org uses PAC files + chained proxies, be careful with domain-based bypass rules — ensure PAC resolves to bypass before the inspector stage. PAC ordering issues caused us similar tickets before.

acme_ops: Smoke passed. No more 502/401s. We're closing the ticket after we get a follow-up config doc.

maya_support: I'll open a short KB doc with the checklist and the common proxy rules we see (TLS passthrough, header-preserve, allowlist IPs). Posting link when ready.

acme_ops: Appreciated.

sre-bot: [update] INC-2026 resolved (root cause: TLS inspection + header stripping).
